title_as_printed: Experimental Values of Density, Viscosity, and Speed of Sound of the Geothermal Fluids as a Function of Temperature at Atmospheric Pressure

footnotes_as_printed.c: DSA 5000M; standard uncertainties, u, are (DMA4500) u(T) = 0.01 K; u(rho) = 0.00025%; (SVM3000) u(T) = 0.005 K; u(rho) = 0.01%; u(eta) = 0.17%; (DSA 5000M) u(rho) = 0.005% (or 0.002 kg m-3); u(c) = 0.05% (or 0.5 m s-1), (level of confidence = 95%).

pressure_note: atmospheric pressure, P0 = 0.101 MPa (text p.237; table title 'at Atmospheric Pressure')

value.what: density of the geothermal brine (SVM 3000 Stabinger viscodensimeter)

value2.what: dynamic viscosity of the brine, SVM 3000

composition.other_species: Natural geothermal brine, Kayakent/Kizlyar field (Dagestan, south Russia); composition by ICP-OES and ion chromatography, Table 1 (mg/L), 'mineralization' from the text 0.89 (No. 4), 1.07 (No. 5), 0.89 (No. 6), 6.34 (No. 17T) g/L is total dissolved solids, not practical salinity of seawater. Not seawater: sulfate/bicarbonate-type natural brine, analyses not charge balanced (no alkalinity); composition not representable in the six-ion set. No. 4 (pH 8.2): Na 228, K 11.2, Ca 56.7, Mg 18.7, Si 18.4, S 118, Cl 67, SO4 369.0, NO3 <0.1. No. 5 (pH 8.2): Na 458, K 3.4, Ca 1.2, Mg 0.4, Si 13.9, S 124, Cl 68.5, SO4 391.5. No. 6 (pH 7.2): Na 556, K 9.27, Ca 8.3, Mg 5.7, Si 12.1, S 1.4, Cl 280, NO3 9.3, SO4 <0.1. No. 17T (pH 7.7): Na 2410, K 71.7, Ca 50.7, Mg 9.5, Si 32.4, S 62.6, Cl 3507, NO3 6.1, SO4 175. Also B, Ba, Li, Sr, Se traces and dissolved gases (N2, CO2, CH4) in the live fluids; samples filtered (2 um), collected at 332-335 K; sample 6 and 17T gas mostly N2, 4 and 5 ~44% N2 and ~53% CO2.

volume_basis_evidence: density in kg m-3; no per-volume concentration quantity
notes: Table 3 prints three side-by-side blocks (a DMA4500; b SVM3000; c DSA 5000M) per sample with own temperature columns; written as table_3_group1..3 (one per instrument), each stacked with one label row per sample (No. 4, 5, 6, 17T). Footnote letters a/b/c (instrument) removed from headers and the instrument added to the header text instead. Salinity values in label-row sets are the 'mineralization' from the text (0.89, 1.07, 0.89, 6.34 g/L), not a table column.
quality_remarks: Composition held: the earlier salinity sets (g/L mineralization) were removed because the builder would read them as reference-seawater salinity, which is wrong for these natural Na-SO4 / Na-Cl brines. Dissolved native gas (N2, CO2, CH4) present; no gas release below 343 K (text), so gas is left blank.
